nodes.title: Revenue Recognition
nodes.heading: Revenue Recognition
nodes.start_phrase: We generate revenue p rimarily from the sale of products and services, both as a principal and as an agent.
nodes.summary:
- Self-insurance: Company uses a mix of third-party insurance and internal risk management; self-insured liabilities totaled $129 million at Feb. 2, 2019 ($69 million accrued, $60 million long-term) vs. $131 million at Feb. 3, 2018 ($67 million accrued, $64 million long-term).
- Income taxes: Uses the asset-and-liability method; recognizes deferred tax assets/liabilities for basis differences and carryforwards, with valuation allowances when needed. Applies an annual effective tax rate adjusted for permanent differences, audit outcomes, and discrete events (e.g., law changes, settlements). Tax returns are audited by multiple jurisdictions; uncertain tax positions are recorded and adjusted upon settlement, statute expiration, or new information. Unrecognized tax benefits (including penalties and interest) are presented in Long-term liabilities and reflected in income tax expense.
- Accrued liabilities: Major components include non-income tax liabilities, advertising accruals, income tax accruals, loyalty program liabilities, rent-related liabilities, and sales return reserves.
- Long-term liabilities: Major components include unrecognized tax benefits, income tax liabilities, rent-related liabilities, and self-insurance reserves.
- Foreign currency: Assets and liabilities translated at balance sheet date rates (one-month lag for certain operations); results and cash flows at average rates; translation adjustments recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income; transaction gains/losses recorded in SG&A and were not significant.
- Revenue recognition: Recognizes revenue when control transfers to the customer, net of sales/usage taxes and net of expected refunds/returns (with related cost of sales reduction). Defers revenue for unsatisfied performance obligations in multi-element arrangements.
- Product revenue: Recognized at a point in time—at in-store sale when customer receives goods; for store-paid home deliveries upon delivery; for online orders upon delivery or customer pick-up. Delivery fees recognized when delivery completes. Generally records gross revenue as principal; records net commission revenue as agent for certain activation-based software licenses and third-party stored-value cards. Assurance-type warranties on exclusive brands are not separate performance obligations.
- Services (principal): Revenue for installation, setup, troubleshooting, repairs, consultations, and classes recognized when service is completed. Technical support memberships (terms one month to three years) recognized over time based on usage patterns; no significant financing component; uses portfolio approach, standalone selling price estimates or cost-plus, and utilization estimates; defaults to ratable recognition when history is insufficient.
- Services (agent): Sells extended hardware protection plans underwritten by third parties; recognizes fixed net commissions at the point in time when related product revenue is recognized and may receive profit-sharing payments.

nodes.title: Product Revenue
nodes.heading: Product Revenue
nodes.start_phrase: Product revenue is recogniz ed when control passes, which generally occurs at a point in time when the customer completes a transaction in the store and receivesthe merchandise.
nodes.summary:
- Focuses on revenue recognition policies under contracts with customers, including treatment of multiple performance obligations and deferral of revenue until obligations are satisfied.
- Product revenue: recognized when control transfers to the customer—generally at point of sale in-store; upon delivery for items paid in-store but delivered later; for online orders, upon delivery to the customer or upon in-store pickup when the customer takes possession. Delivery fees are included in the transaction price and recognized when delivery is complete, using delivery data at the contract level.
- Principal vs. agent: typically acts as principal for physical product sales (recognizes revenue on a gross basis). For activation-based software licenses and third-party stored-value cards, acts as agent and recognizes fixed commission revenue net of amounts remitted, with control passing when access to content is provided.
- Warranties on exclusive brand products are assurance-type (not separate performance obligations).
- Services when acting as principal: installation, setup, troubleshooting, repairs, consultations, and classes are recognized when the service is completed; payment is typically at point of sale or upon completion. Service contracts with vendors and underwriters (e.g., factory warranty repairs) are included.
- Technical support membership contracts: company is responsible for fulfillment; terms range from one month to three years; multiple performance obligations; payment due at start; no significant financing component. Revenue recognized over time on a usage-based input method reflecting historical utilization and discount usage; when insufficient history exists, recognized ratably over the contract term.
- Judgments include portfolio application level, determining standalone selling prices for bundled obligations (including use of a cost-plus approach), and estimating current/future usage patterns across customer portfolios.
- Services when acting as agent: sells third-party underwritten hardware protection plans (one month to five years); underwriter bears the risk and fulfills coverage. Company records fixed net commissions as revenue at a point in time when related product revenue is recognized and may receive profit-sharing payments.

nodes.title: Services - When we are the principal
nodes.heading: Services - When we are the prin cipal
nodes.start_phrase: We recognize servic e revenue for installation, set-up, software troubleshooting, product repair, consultation and educational classes once the service is completed,as this is when the customer has the ability to direct the use of and obtain the benefits of the service or serviced product.
nodes.summary:
- Revenue recognition follows satisfaction of performance obligations; revenue for unsatisfied obligations is deferred until control transfers or services are completed (per Note 8, Revenue Recognition).
- Product revenue: recognized at a point in time when control passes—generally at in-store purchase, upon delivery for items paid in-store then delivered, upon delivery for shipped online orders, and upon customer pickup for in-store pickup orders. Delivery fees are included in the transaction price and recognized when delivery is complete, using contract-level delivery data.
- Principal vs. agent: Company is generally principal and records product sales on a gross basis. For activation-based software licenses and third‑party stored‑value cards, the company acts as an agent and recognizes fixed commission revenue net of amounts due to third parties when access is provided.
- Warranties on exclusive brands are assurance-type and not separate performance obligations.
- Services (principal): Revenue for installations, setup, troubleshooting, repairs, consultations, and classes is recognized when the service is completed; payment is typically at point of sale or upon completion. Service contracts involve retail customers, merchandise vendors (factory warranty repairs), and third‑party underwriters.
- Technical support memberships (principal): Company is responsible for fulfillment; contracts run one month to three years, paid upfront, with no significant financing component. Revenue is recognized over time on a usage basis reflecting historical utilization and discounts. Judgments include portfolio scoping, standalone selling price allocation (or cost‑plus), and estimating usage patterns; if history is insufficient, recognize ratably over the term.
- Services (agent): Hardware protection plans (extended warranties) sold on behalf of third‑party underwriters (who bear risk and fulfill) have terms of one month to five years, paid at sale. The company records fixed net commissions as revenue at the point in time when the related product revenue is recognized and may receive profit‑sharing payments.

nodes.title: Services - When we are the agent
nodes.heading: Services - When we are the agent
nodes.start_phrase: We sell various hardware p rotection plans to customers that provide extended warranty coverage on their device purchases.
nodes.summary:
- Explains overall revenue recognition approach: revenue is recognized when control of goods or services transfers; amounts related to unsatisfied performance obligations are deferred. Principal-versus-agent assessments determine gross or net reporting.
- Product revenue:
  - In-store sales recognized at point of sale; for items sold in-store but delivered later, revenue recognized upon delivery.
  - Online sales recognized upon delivery to customer or upon in-store pickup when customer takes possession.
  - Delivery fees are included in transaction price and recognized upon delivery; delivery data at the contract level informs timing.
  - Generally reported gross as principal; certain activation-based software licenses and third-party stored-value cards are reported net as agent, with revenue recognized upon providing access.
  - Assurance-type warranties on exclusive brands are not separate performance obligations.
- Services when the company is principal:
  - Installation, setup, troubleshooting, repair, consultations, and classes recognized at completion; payment typically at point of sale or upon completion.
  - Technical support memberships (terms one month to three years) include multiple performance obligations, billed upfront, and recognized over time using a usage-based input method; no significant financing component.
  - Significant judgments: portfolio application level, standalone selling price estimation (including cost-plus), and usage pattern estimation; ratable recognition used when history is insufficient.
- Services when the company is agent:
  - Hardware protection/extended warranty plans (terms one month to five years) underwritten by third parties: fixed net commissions recognized at the related product revenue point in time.
  - Profit-sharing from underwriters (variable consideration) recognized when unconstrained using expected value method, typically in fiscal Q4; payments occur the following fiscal year.
  - Service and commission revenues from extended warranties were 2.0%, 2.0%, and 2.2% of revenue in fiscal 2019, 2018, and 2017, including profit-share revenue of $10m, $68m, and $133m, respectively.
  - Mobile carrier service contracts: fixed commissions recognized at activation; cash received 30–60 days later; revenues recorded net of expected cancellations based on historical rates.
- Credit card programs:
  - Third-party banks issue and own receivables; company provides brand license and marketing and acts as agent.
  - Eligible for program profit-share (variable consideration) recognized over time using the most-likely-amount method when a significant reversal is not probable; payments are quarterly.
- Gift cards:
  - Sold in stores, online, and via partners; no expiration.
  - Revenue recognized upon redemption; breakage recognized consistent with redemption patterns (over 90% of redemptions and breakage recognition occur within one year).
  - Judgments include grouping level, redemption patterns, and ultimate breakage estimates.
  - Breakage income was $34m, $40m, and $37m in fiscal 2019, 2018, and 2017, respectively.
- Sales incentives:
  - Incentives earned with a purchase (e.g., gift cards or future-use coupons) are material rights and separate performance obligations; defer relative standalone selling price based on expected redemptions; recognize upon redemption or when not expected to be redeemed. Judgments include grouping, redemption patterns, and non-redemption estimates.
  - Coupons not earned with a purchase (targeted marketing) are not performance obligations and reduce the transaction price when redeemed.

nodes.title: Credit Card Revenue
nodes.heading: Credit Card Revenue
nodes.start_phrase: We offer promotional financing and credit cards issued by third-party banks that manage and directly extend credit to our customers.
nodes.summary:
- Describes revenue recognition policies for variable consideration tied to performance-based profit-sharing and commissions.
- Extended warranties: Company earns service and commission revenues from warranty sales, including a profit-share that is a form of variable consideration. Profit-share is recognized as revenue using the expected value method once annual claims experience is known, typically in the fiscal fourth quarter, with payment in the subsequent fiscal year. Warranty-related service and commission revenues were 2.0%, 2.0%, and 2.2% of revenue in fiscal 2019, 2018, and 2017, including profit-share of $10 million, $68 million, and $133 million, respectively.
- Mobile carrier commissions: Fixed activation commissions are recognized at a point in time upon contract sale and customer activation. Cash collection generally occurs 30–60 days after activation. Commissions are subject to clawback for customer cancellations; revenue is recorded net of expected cancellations based on historical rates.
- Credit card programs: Third-party banks issue promotional financing and credit cards; the company licenses its brand and facilitates applications, acts as an agent, and holds no customer receivables. The company earns a profit-share from certain banking partners based on annual program performance, with quarterly payments. This variable consideration is recognized over time using the most likely amount method when a significant revenue reversal is not probable, typically assessed quarterly.
- Gift cards: Revenue is recognized upon redemption. Breakage is recognized based on historical redemption patterns and applicable laws, using a method consistent with redemption behavior; over 90% of redemptions (and breakage recognition) occur within one year of issuance. Breakage income was $34 million, $40 million, and $37 million in fiscal 2019, 2018, and 2017, respectively. Judgment applies to grouping, redemption patterns, and ultimate unredeemed values.
- Sales incentives: Incentives earned only with a purchase (e.g., a gift card at purchase or future-use coupon) are treated as a material right and a separate performance obligation. The relative standalone selling price is deferred as a contract liability based on projected redemptions and recognized when redeemed or when not expected to be redeemed, with judgment in grouping, redemption patterns, and expected non-redemptions. Coupons not earned with a purchase (e.g., targeted marketing) are not a performance obligation and reduce the transaction price when redeemed.

nodes.title: Best Buy Gift Cards
nodes.heading: Best Buy Gift Cards
nodes.start_phrase: We sell Best Buy gift cards to ou r customers in our retail stores, online and through select third parties.
nodes.summary:
- Revenue recognition for profit-sharing on extended warranties:
  - Profit share is variable consideration tied to portfolio profitability; the company does not share in portfolio losses.
  - Recognized as revenue when uncertainty is resolved using the expected value method, typically in fiscal Q4 once calendar-year claims experience is known; cash paid the following fiscal year.
  - Service and commission revenue from extended warranties was 2.0%, 2.0%, and 2.2% of total revenue in fiscal 2019, 2018, and 2017, including profit-share revenue of $10M, $68M, and $133M, respectively.

- Commissions from mobile network carriers:
  - Fixed commissions for selling/activating service contracts recognized at a point in time upon sale and customer activation.
  - Payments typically received within 30–60 days after control transfers.
  - Commissions are subject to chargebacks for customer cancellations; revenue reported net of expected cancellations based on historical rates.

- Credit card program revenue:
  - Third-party banks issue and own customer receivables; the company acts as agent, providing brand license, marketing, and application facilitation.
  - Eligible for profit share based on annual program performance; payments made quarterly based on forecasts.
  - Recognized over time using the most likely amount method when a significant reversal is not probable; assessed quarterly.

- Gift cards:
  - No expiration; revenue recognized upon redemption.
  - Breakage recognized consistent with redemption patterns, based on historical data and jurisdictional rules; over 90% of redemptions and breakage recognition occur within one year of issuance.
  - Judgment applied to grouping, redemption patterns, and estimating ultimate breakage.
  - Breakage income was $34M (fiscal 2019), $40M (2018), and $37M (2017).

- Sales incentives:
  - Incentives earned with a purchase (e.g., gift cards at purchase or instant savings coupons for future use) are material rights and treated as separate performance obligations.
  - Deferred at relative standalone selling price based on expected redemptions; recognized when redeemed or when redemption is not expected.
  - Judgment required for grouping, forecasting redemption patterns, and estimating non-redemptions.
  - Coupons not earned with a purchase (e.g., targeted marketing) are not performance obligations and reduce the transaction price when redeemed.

nodes.title: Sales Incentives
nodes.heading: Sales Incentives
nodes.start_phrase: We frequently offer sales ince ntives that entitle our customers to receive a gift card at the time of purchase or an instant savings coupon that can be redeemedtowards a future purchase.
nodes.summary:
- Revenue recognition for extended warranties and related profit-share arrangements:
  - Profit-share is variable consideration based on portfolio profitability; Best Buy does not share in portfolio losses.
  - Recognized using the expected value method when annual claims experience is known (typically fiscal Q4); cash received the following fiscal year.
  - Service and commission revenues from extended warranties were 2.0%, 2.0%, and 2.2% of revenue in fiscal 2019, 2018, and 2017, including profit-share of $10M, $68M, and $133M, respectively.

- Commissions from mobile network carriers:
  - Fixed commissions for selling/activating service contracts recognized at a point in time upon customer activation.
  - Payments generally received within 30–60 days post-activation.
  - Commissions subject to chargebacks for cancellations; revenue reported net of expected cancellations based on historical rates.

- Credit card revenue (promotional financing and co-branded cards):
  - Programs run by third-party banks; Best Buy acts as agent and does not hold receivables.
  - Eligible for profit-share based on annual program performance; variable consideration recognized over time using the most likely amount when a significant reversal is not probable; payments occur quarterly.

- Gift cards:
  - No expiration; revenue recognized upon redemption.
  - Breakage recognized consistent with redemption patterns based on historical data and jurisdictional rules; over 90% of redemptions (and breakage recognition) occur within one year.
  - Breakage income: $34M (fiscal 2019), $40M (2018), $37M (2017).

- Sales incentives:
  - Incentives earned with a purchase (e.g., gift cards at purchase, future-use coupons) are material rights and separate performance obligations.
  - Relative standalone selling price deferred as a contract liability based on projected redemptions; revenue recognized when redeemed or when redemption is not expected.
  - Coupons not earned with a purchase (marketing offers) reduce the transaction price when redeemed.
  - Significant judgment in grouping incentives, estimating redemption patterns, and expected breakage.

- Customer loyalty programs:
  - Points earned on purchases or via co-branded cards create material rights/performance obligations.
  - Standalone selling price of points deferred in accrued liabilities based on projected redemptions; revenue recognized over time as certificates are estimated to be redeemed.
  - Certificates typically expire 2–12 months after issuance; estimates rely on historical redemption data.

- Expense classification:
  - Cost of Goods Sold includes product costs; inbound and inter-facility freight; vendor allowances not tied to specific, incremental, identifiable costs; cash discounts; services-related payroll/parts; inventory losses; markdowns; customer shipping/handling; distribution network operating costs and depreciation.
  - Selling, General and Administrative includes payroll/benefits for retail and corporate; occupancy/maintenance; depreciation/amortization; advertising; vendor allowances that reimburse specific, incremental, identifiable costs; tender costs (bank charges, interchange fees); charitable contributions; outside/outsourced services; long-lived asset impairments; and other admin costs (supplies, travel, lodging).

- Vendor allowances:
  - Funds from vendors (volume-based, advertising, product placement) generally recorded as a reduction of cost of sales when associated inventory is sold.
  - If not tied to purchase/sales volumes, recognized ratably over the promotional performance period.

nodes.title: Customer Loyalty Programs
nodes.heading: Customer Loyalty Programs
nodes.start_phrase: We have customer loyal ty programs which allow members to earn points for each purchase completed with us or when using our co-branded credit cards.
nodes.summary:
- Describes the company’s customer loyalty programs: members earn points on purchases and co-branded credit card use; points convert to certificates redeemable at Best Buy stores with expirations typically 2–12 months based on membership level.
- Explains accounting for loyalty programs under revenue recognition: the programs provide a material right and are treated as performance obligations; the standalone selling price of points is deferred in Accrued liabilities based on projected redemptions; revenue is recognized over time as certificates are estimated to be redeemed; estimates rely on historical redemption data and involve judgment.
- Outlines expense classification policies:
  - Cost of goods sold includes product costs; freight from vendors to distribution centers and from distribution centers to stores; certain vendor allowances and cash discounts; service-related payroll/benefits and parts; physical inventory losses; markdowns; customer shipping/handling; and distribution network operating costs (payroll, occupancy, depreciation).
  - Selling, general and administrative expenses include payroll/benefits for retail and corporate staff; facility occupancy/maintenance; depreciation and amortization; advertising; vendor allowances that reimburse specific, incremental, identifiable costs; tender costs (bank and interchange fees); charitable contributions; outsourced services; long-lived asset impairments; and other administrative costs (supplies, travel, lodging).
- Summarizes vendor allowances: received from vendors based on purchase/sales volumes and for advertising/placement; recognized as a reduction of cost of sales when related inventory is sold; if not tied to purchase/sales volumes, recognized ratably over the promotion period.

nodes.title: Cost of Goods Sold and Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
nodes.heading: Cost of Goods Sold and Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
nodes.start_phrase: The following table illust rates the primary costs classified in each major expense category:
nodes.summary:
- Describes Best Buy’s customer loyalty programs: members earn points on purchases and co-branded credit card use; points convert to certificates redeemable in Best Buy stores with expirations typically 2–12 months based on membership level.
- Explains revenue recognition for loyalty programs under ASC 606: loyalty benefits are a material right and treated as separate performance obligations; the relative standalone selling price of points is deferred in accrued liabilities based on projected redemptions; revenue is recognized over time as certificates are estimated to be redeemed; estimates rely on historical redemption data and involve judgment.
- Details cost classifications:
  - Cost of Goods Sold includes product costs, inbound and outbound freight, certain vendor allowances, cash discounts, service labor and parts, physical inventory losses, markdowns, customer shipping/handling, and distribution network operating costs (payroll, occupancy, depreciation).
  - Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) includes payroll/benefits for retail and corporate staff, facility occupancy/maintenance, depreciation and amortization, advertising, vendor allowances that reimburse specific incremental identifiable costs, tender/processing fees, charitable contributions, outside services, long-lived asset impairments, and other admin costs (supplies, travel, lodging).
- Outlines accounting for vendor allowances: funds received from vendors via volume-based programs and for advertising/placement are recognized as reductions of cost of sales when related inventory is sold; if not tied to purchase/sales volumes, they are recognized ratably over the promotion’s performance period.

nodes.title: Vendor Allowances
nodes.heading: Vendor Allowances
nodes.start_phrase: We receive funds from certain vendors through a variety of programs and arrangements, primarily in the form of purchases-based or sales-based volumes and forproduct advertising and pla cement in our stores.
nodes.summary:
- Describes Best Buy’s customer loyalty programs, where members earn points on purchases and co‑branded credit card use, redeemable as certificates at Best Buy stores. Certificates typically expire in 2–12 months. The programs are treated as material rights and performance obligations; the relative standalone selling price of points expected to be redeemed is deferred in accrued liabilities, with revenue recognized over time based on estimated redemptions. Estimates rely on historical redemption data and involve judgment.

- Details the classification of expenses between Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) and Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A):
  - COGS includes product costs, freight to distribution centers and to stores, certain vendor allowances and cash discounts, service labor and parts, physical inventory losses, markdowns, customer shipping/handling, and distribution network operating costs.
  - SG&A includes payroll/benefits for retail and corporate, occupancy/maintenance, depreciation/amortization, advertising, vendor allowances that reimburse specific identifiable costs, tender costs (bank charges, interchange fees), charitable contributions, outside services, long‑lived asset impairments, and other admin costs (supplies, travel, lodging).

- Explains vendor allowances: funds from vendors (volume-based or for advertising/placement) are generally recorded as reductions of cost of sales when related inventory is sold; if not tied to purchase/sales volumes, they are recognized ratably over the promotion period; reimbursements of specific, incremental, identifiable costs offset the related expense.

- Outlines advertising cost accounting: included in SG&A and expensed over the period the advertisement is customer-facing; consists mainly of digital/TV ads, agency fees, and production. Reported advertising expenses were $777 million (fiscal 2019), $776 million (fiscal 2018), and $743 million (fiscal 2017).

- Summarizes stock-based compensation: expense recognized at fair value over the service period; straight-line for most awards; graded attribution (front‑loaded) for performance awards with graded vesting; additional details referenced in Shareholders’ Equity note.

- Provides acquisition details for GreatCall, Inc. (October 1, 2018): acquired for net cash consideration of $787 million. GreatCall provides connected health services and devices for aging consumers, aligning with Best Buy’s health and wellness strategy. Accounted for under the acquisition method; goodwill assigned to the Domestic segment and not tax-deductible. $13 million in transaction costs recorded in SG&A (fiscal 2019). Operations post-acquisition included in the Domestic segment and Services revenue; acquisition not material to overall results. Purchase price allocation (post-measurement adjustments): total assets acquired $920 million (including $490 million goodwill and $373 million intangible assets); liabilities assumed $125 million; total purchase price $795 million, less $8 million cash acquired, yielding $787 million net consideration.

nodes.title: Advertising Costs

- Vendor reimbursements: Specific, incremental, and identifiable costs incurred to sell a vendor’s products are recorded as offsets to the related expense when incurred.
- Advertising costs: Included in SG&A and expensed over the period the advertisement is customer-facing; primarily digital/TV, agency fees, and production. Advertising expense was $777 million (fiscal 2019), $776 million (fiscal 2018), and $743 million (fiscal 2017).
- Stock-based compensation: Expense recognized at fair value over the required service period; generally straight-line, with graded attribution (front-loaded) for performance awards that vest on a graded basis. Additional details referenced in Note 7, Shareholders’ Equity.

- Nonrecurring fair value measurements and impairments:
  - Long‑lived assets (property and equipment), goodwill, and other intangibles are remeasured to fair value only upon impairment; otherwise carried at cost.
  - Impairment losses are recorded in SG&A (non‑restructuring) or Restructuring charges, as applicable.

  - Counterparty credit risk is mitigated by transacting with investment‑grade financial institutions; no derivatives contain credit risk‑related contingent features.

nodes.title: Derivative Instruments
nodes.heading: 5. Derivative Instruments
nodes.start_phrase: We manage our economic and transaction exposure to certain risks by using foreign currency derivative instruments and interest rate swaps.
nodes.summary:
- Fair value measurements and hierarchy: mutual fund investments classified as Level 1; interest rate swap derivatives measured using observable inputs (e.g., LIBOR) and classified as Level 2.
- Nonrecurring fair value measurements: applied to tangible fixed assets, goodwill, and other intangibles upon impairment; not adjusted to fair value unless impaired. All such remeasurements used Level 3 unobservable inputs.
- Impairments (continuing operations): in fiscal 2019, $9 million impairment of property and equipment (non-restructuring) with $1 million remaining net carrying value; in fiscal 2018, $10 million total impairments ($9 million non-restructuring, $1 million restructuring) with no remaining net carrying value. Fair values estimated primarily via discounted cash flow models using forecasts of revenues, expenses, capital expenditures, and appropriate discount rates; for restructuring-related assets, no future cash flows assumed and nominal sale values expected.
- Fair value of financial instruments: cash, receivables, accounts payable, and other payables approximate carrying values (would be Level 1 if measured at fair value). Other investments held at cost approximate fair value. Long-term debt fair value referenced in a separate debt note.
- Derivative risk management: use of foreign currency forwards and interest rate swaps to reduce volatility in earnings, cash flows, and net assets; no trading/speculative use; counterparties are investment grade; all derivatives recorded at fair value with hedge effectiveness assessed when hedge accounting is applied.
- Net investment hedges: foreign exchange forwards (terms up to 12 months) used to hedge a portion of the Canadian net investment; changes in fair value recognized in other comprehensive income as a component of foreign currency translation, with limited reclassification to earnings upon (substantially) complete liquidation.
- Interest rate swaps: receive-fixed, pay-variable swaps designated as fair value hedges of fixed-rate Notes (2018, 2021, 2028) using the shortcut method; changes in derivative fair value offset by changes in carrying value of the hedged debt, resulting in no impact on earnings.
- Derivatives not designated as hedges: foreign currency forwards used to manage remeasurement exposure on recognized non-functional currency balances (terms up to 12 months); gains and losses recorded directly in earnings.
- Derivative balances: as of February 2, 2019, assets included $26 million (interest rate swaps) and $0 for net investment hedges; liabilities totaled $1 million (interest rate swaps), with $0 for net investment hedges and $0 for non-designated FX forwards. Prior year (February 3, 2018) balances included $2 million assets (net investment hedges) and $13 million liabilities (including $7 million net investment hedges, $5 million interest rate swaps, and $1 million non-designated FX forwards).
- OCI impact of net investment hedges: pre-tax gain of $21 million in fiscal 2019 versus a pre-tax loss of $14 million in fiscal 2018.

nodes.title: Net Investment Hedges
nodes.heading: Net Investment Hedges
nodes.start_phrase: We use foreign exchange fo rward contracts to hedge against the effect of Canadian dollar exchange rate fluctuations on a portion of our net investment in ourCanadian operations.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of the company’s derivative and hedge accounting framework, including documentation at inception, identification of hedged items, and risk management objectives and strategies. Notes that some derivatives are not designated as hedging instruments.
- Net investment hedges:
  - Use of foreign exchange forward contracts to hedge Canadian dollar exposure on a portion of the company’s net investment in Canadian operations, with terms up to 12 months.
  - Accounting: changes in fair value recognized in other comprehensive income (OCI) as a component of foreign currency translation to offset changes in the translated value of the net investment; amounts reclassified to earnings only upon complete or substantially complete liquidation of the investment.
  - Amounts excluded from hedge effectiveness are recognized in net earnings.
- Interest rate swaps:
  - “Receive fixed, pay variable” swaps used to mitigate interest rate fluctuations on fixed-rate debt (previously 2018 Notes; currently 2021 and 2028 Notes).
  - Designated as fair value hedges using the shortcut method because critical terms and notionals match the hedged debt; changes in derivative fair value offset by adjustments to the carrying value of the debt, resulting in no impact on earnings from fair value changes.
- Derivatives not designated as hedging instruments:
  - Foreign currency forwards used to manage FX risk on recognized receivables and payables in non-functional currencies, generally with terms up to 12 months.
  - Gains and losses recognized directly in net earnings.
- Summary of derivative balances (fair values):
  - Assets at Feb 2, 2019 vs. Feb 3, 2018: $26 million vs. $2 million, driven by interest rate swaps ($26 million in other assets in 2019; none in 2018). Net investment hedge asset declined to $0 from $2 million.
  - Liabilities at Feb 2, 2019 vs. Feb 3, 2018: $1 million vs. $13 million, including interest rate swaps ($1 million vs. $5 million), net investment hedges ($0 vs. $7 million), and non-designated FX forwards ($0 vs. $1 million).
- Effects on OCI for derivatives designated as net investment hedges:
  - 2019: pre-tax gain of $21 million.
  - 2018: pre-tax loss of $14 million.

nodes.title: Interest Rate Swaps

nodes.summary:
- Focus: Company’s use of derivatives and hedge accounting, including documentation at inception, risk management objectives/strategies, and treatment of derivatives both designated and not designated as hedges.
- Net investment hedges: Use of foreign exchange forward contracts (terms up to 12 months) to hedge Canadian dollar exposure on a portion of net investment in Canadian operations. Changes in fair value recorded in other comprehensive income (OCI) within foreign currency translation to offset changes in the net investment; amounts reclassified to earnings only upon complete or substantially complete liquidation. Amounts excluded from hedge effectiveness are recognized in net earnings. Reported pre-tax OCI impact: $21 gain in 2019 vs. $(14) loss in 2018.
- Interest rate swaps: “Receive fixed, pay variable” swaps used to hedge fixed-rate debt (prior 2018 Notes; currently 2021 and 2028 Notes). Designated as fair value hedges under the shortcut method due to matching critical terms and notional amounts. Accounting: changes in derivative fair value offset by changes to carrying value of the hedged debt; no impact on Consolidated Statements of Earnings from these fair value changes.
- Derivatives not designated as hedging instruments: Foreign currency forward contracts used to manage FX risk on recognized receivables and payables in non-functional currencies (terms up to 12 months). Gains and losses recognized directly in net earnings.
- Summary of derivative balances (fair values and balance sheet classification):
  - Assets at Feb 2, 2019: $26 million in Other assets (interest rate swaps); $0 for net investment hedges. At Feb 3, 2018: $2 million in Other current assets (net investment hedges); $0 for interest rate swaps.

At Feb 3, 2018: $7 million for net investment hedges (accrued liabilities), $5 million for interest rate swaps (accrued and long-term), and $1 million for non-designated FX forwards (accrued liabilities).
  - Totals: Assets $26 (2019) vs. $2 (2018); Liabilities $1 (2019) vs. $13 (2018).
- Presentation: Effects of net investment hedge derivatives on OCI are disclosed for fiscal 2019 and 2018.

nodes.title: Derivatives Not Designated as Hedging Instruments
nodes.heading: Derivatives Not Designated as Hedging Instrumen ts
nodes.start_phrase: We use foreign currency f orward contracts to manage the impact of fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates relative to recognized receivable and payablebalances denominated in non functional currencies.

- Net investment hedges: Uses foreign exchange forward contracts (terms up to 12 months) to hedge Canadian dollar exposure on its Canadian net investment. Changes in fair value are recorded in other comprehensive income (OCI) as foreign currency translation; amounts are reclassified to net earnings only upon complete or substantially complete liquidation of the investment. Any amounts excluded from hedge effectiveness are recognized in net earnings.
- Interest rate swaps: Employs receive-fixed, pay-variable swaps to hedge fixed-rate debt (previously 2018 Notes; currently 2021 and 2028 Notes). These are accounted for as fair value hedges using the shortcut method because critical terms match the hedged debt; changes in derivative fair value are offset by adjustments to the carrying value of the debt, resulting in no impact on earnings from these fair value changes.

- Summary of derivative balances (fair values): At February 2, 2019 versus February 3, 2018, assets totaled $26 million vs. $2 million (primarily interest rate swaps in other assets), and liabilities totaled $1 million vs. $13 million (declines in net investment hedge and interest rate swap liabilities; no hedge designation FX forwards declined to zero).
